method: Independent source-first mathematical comparison of supplied TeX spans, Lean types, definitions and relevant proof bodies. No independent Lean kernel replay; report compilation/axiom print provenance remains unverified. One bounded local static inventory/numerical diagnostic is recorded with exact command and stdout under evidence.
population_rule: C1-C6 are ordinal identifiers for the six claims in INPUT/SCORE-POPULATION.json; every report-claim pair appears exactly once. Exploratory records cannot satisfy the primary gate.

summary.rationale: Both reports support the same six registered correspondences. Their headings use finding for positive controls, but neither establishes a source/formal discrepancy in the registered population. Training-accountant and replay abstentions are warranted exploratory coverage limits, not source refutations.

ratings.interpreted_assertion: With zero initial history and unit Euclidean clipping, each release sums exactly the scheduled clipped queries, adds independent Gaussian noise of standard deviation sigma, and retains each user schedule until the full adaptive transcript is formed.

evidence.assumptions_domains_quantifiers: Arbitrary record type with decidable equality; finite-set dataset; T>0; 0<=k<=T; any finite output dimension; measurable history-dependent query; positive source noise scale. The definition additionally permits arbitrary clipping radius, initial history, k and real sigma; correspondence uses radius 1, zero initial history and the source domain.
evidence.source_type_definition_proof_analysis: TrainingMechanism.lean:77-130 computes the scheduled sum, recursively binds a fresh bsrGaussianMeasure with the same assignment argument, and sums assignment weights only outside the entire T-step law. AdaptiveTranscript.lean supplies measurable_history and zeroAdaptiveReleaseHistory. Unwritten coordinates of the infinite history are public zero, so inspecting the ambient history adds no private future input. The returned object is a padded history-valued law; this definition does not itself prove the finite-vector projection identity or a privacy theorem.
